newsitem.title: USA: Masco sees record 1997 sales, earnings.
newsitem.headline: Masco sees record 1997 sales, earnings.

text.p: Masco Corp Chairman Richard Manoogian said the company can achieve record sales and earnings from continuing operations in 1997 if the economy continues to grow at a moderate rate.

The maker of building and home improvement products, best known for its Delta and Peerless faucets and Merillat and KraftMaid cabinetry reported a 35 percent increase in first quarter net income to $83.5 million, or $0.52 a share, from $62 million, or $0.39 a share, a year earlier.
Masco said its 1997 first quarter earnings benefitted from increased product sales and interest income from proceeds of the 1996 divestiture of the home furnishings business, M.
"Our improved first quarter performance reflects our focus on our core businesses to generate sales and earnings growth both internally and through acquisitions," Manoogian said in a statement.

"We also continue to emphasize cost containment to enhance profitability," Manoogian said. "We remain committed to increasing shareholder value, and if the economy continues to grow at a moderate rate, we expect to achieve record sales and earnings from continuing operations for the full year 1997."
Aided by recent acquisitions, Masco said its Kitchen and Bath Products Segment sales increased 14 percent in the first quarter of 1997 to $679 million from $596 million a year earlier.

First quarter sales of the Other Specialty Products Segment were $175 million in 1997, an increase of only four percent over net sales of $168 million in 1996, primarily because the strength of the U.S. dollar against European currencies adversely affected the translation of European sales into dollars.
